goals.en:
Upon the successful completion of the course, students will be able to:
1- Understand the historical factors and global forces that shape health.
2- Discuss health in its dynamic interaction with sociocultural and political dimensions that shape individual’s quality of life
3- Compare different definitions of health and explain their differences.
4- Understand the double burden of diseases (communicable and non-communicable) and health inequalities in relation to time and place.
5- Write analytical reflections and present their ideas in an academically sound way.
6- Effectively communicate and present their knowledge to their peers using online and virtual means.
7- Effectively collaborate with one another to strengthen peer and collective learning.
8- Acquire new core skills and deal with challenges such as lack of structure, uncertainties or confusion while expanding their academic learning.
9- Design and run a health campaign.

description.en:
Introduction to Global Health is one of the foundation courses, aiming to introduce students to
basic concepts, theories and challenges of global health. Throughout the course, students learn
about the historical development of health and improve their understanding on socioeconomic,
political and structural factors that shape health as a quality of life. The course has several
characteristics:
- it is an interdisciplinary course,
- it places a strong emphasis on the assessment of contrasting and diverse views in explaining global health issues,
- interactive learning is the centerpiece of the course,
- throughout the course students navigate between comfort zone and growth zone in their learning curve.

The foundation course includes six themes:
1) Historical development, time and place 
– Under this component, we critically study the historical development and how it shaped health and medicine.

2) Health definition, theories, concepts and tools
– This component sheds light on the range of definitions for health. We introduce and discuss different health theories - and the new
generations of health theories in particular.

3) Health and populations 
– Here, we deconstruct population groups according to the individual, social and environmental factors that influence the quality of their life and
health.

4) Global health leadership and governance 
– We learn about different actors and stakeholders that contribute to health as a capability. Global health targets, indicators and challenges are also introduced and discussed.

5) Health campaigns and community days 
– This is the applied component of the course. In specific classes, we learn how to design a health campaign on a specific topic, plan strategies and finally run real time community campaigns. Campaigns are very good opportunities for all of us to link academic learning with policy and practice and understand the societal relevance of our knowledge. Through campaigning, we also learn more about the role of different stakeholders (e.g. schools or municipalities) in health promotion. Furthermore, they help us establish team spirit and networks that help us in future courses.

6) SDGs 
- While SDG 3 (Good Health and Wellbeing) is at the heart of this course, other development goals are discussed as well, such as SDG 5 (gender equality) and SDG 10 (reduced inequality).
